q: Is version mein style kaisa hai
a:
- **Tech words English mein hi:** production, staging, deploy, rollback, bottleneck, root cause, trade-off, edge case, scale, latency, retry, timeout, fallback, cache, queue, worker, index, query, transaction, lock, migration, endpoint, token, audit log. Inka Urdu tarjuma nahi kiya, kyunke interview mein aap yehi bolenge.
- **Verbs ka pattern:** English word + karna, lagana, chalana. Jaise "deploy karta hoon", "index laga deta hoon", "worker chala deta hoon".
- **Chhote, bole jaane wale jumle:** "Main sab se pehle check karta hoon...", "Simple si baat hai...", "Trade-off yeh hai...".
- **Structure:** pehle masla, phir wajah, phir fix, phir apni example. Yeh pattern lagbhag har answer par chalta hai.
- Practice ke liye Roman Urdu mein samjhein, lekin final answer interview mein English mein bolne ki practice karein.

q: **Government context:** audit trail, sensitive data (CNIC, police records), role-based access, long-term maintenance, aur vendors ya departments par dependency.
a: **Opening line:** "Maine high-volume, multi-tenant platforms banaye hain jin mein queues, caching aur live dashboards thay. Reliability, security aur delivery tracking ka wohi discipline is program ko chahiye."

q: A. Role, delivery aur HR questions
a:
**Q1. Aap Pakistan Railways ki digital transformation par kyun kaam karna chahte hain?** Answer: Yeh bahut bara public system hai jis ka real impact hai: ticketing, tracking, safety, transparency. Mujhe lambe programs pasand hain jahan sirf quick demo nahi, quality matter karti hai. Aur team lead ke taur par main delivery lead kar chuka hoon.
**Q2. Yeh 3 saal ka contract hai. Hum kaise maanein ke aap tikenge aur motivated rahenge?** Answer: 3 saal ka program mujhe cheezein properly build karne aur production mein chalte dekhne ka moqa deta hai. Mujhe system ko poore cycle mein own karna pasand hai: build, release, support, improve.
**Q3. Developer role mein "IT Operations" ka matlab kya hai?** Answer: Aisa code likhna jise run karna aasan ho: proper logs, health checks, alerts, safe deployments, runbooks aur fast incident response. Jab tak support team feature ko operate na kar sake, tab tak feature done nahi hai.
**Q4. Aap kaise ensure karenge ke development targets poore hon?** Answer: Main program ko modules mein todta hoon, har module ka owner, milestones aur clear "done" criteria. Progress weekly track karta hoon, demos jaldi dikhata hoon, aur risk jis din nazar aaye usi din raise karta hoon. Waqt kam ho to scope cut karta hoon, quality nahi. *Cross-question: Agar target unrealistic ho?* Answer: Main numbers dikhata hoon (tasks, effort, risks) aur options deta hoon: scope kam karein, log barhayen, ya date aage karein. Jo deliver nahi kar sakta, uska wada nahi karta.
**Q5. Aap software ko bug-free kaise rakhte hain?** Answer: Koi software 100 percent bug-free nahi hota, isliye main process banata hoon: code review, critical paths par automated tests, CI checks, staging, safe release, aur release ke baad monitoring. Goal yeh hai ke serious bugs users tak na pohnchein, aur chhote bugs jaldi fix hon.
**Q6. Senior officer testing complete hone se pehle release ka pressure daalein to kya karenge?** Answer: Main risk simple words mein batata hoon: kya toot sakta hai, kis par asar padega. Phir safe option deta hoon: tested core abhi release karein, baqi hold par. Decision aur risk dono email ya document mein likh deta hoon.
**Q7. Kya aap ne government ya large organizations ke saath kaam kiya hai?** Answer: Directly government ke saath nahi. Mera kaam large multi-tenant platforms par raha hai jahan reliability, access control aur audit critical thay. Domain rules main business team ke saath baith kar jaldi seekh leta hoon.
**Q8. Koi project batayen jo aap ne end to end lead kiya (aapki story).** Answer: HOLOIN. Multi-tenant IoT platform: high-volume device data, queues, Docker aur AI service layer. Maine modules plan kiye, code review kiya, slow queries fix ki (10 se 20 minute ki queries indexes, DB-side processing aur latest-value caching se usable hui), aur production issues handle kiye.
**Q9. Alag alag skill levels wali team ko kaise manage karte hain?** Answer: Juniors ko chhote, clear tasks examples ke saath deta hoon, shuru ke tasks par pair karta hoon, aur feedback specific aur polite rakhta hoon. Seniors ko ek module ki ownership deta hoon. Shared checklist rakhta hoon taake sab ki quality ek jaisi ho.
**Q10. PITB teams aur Railways officers (jo technical nahi) ke saath kaise kaam karte hain?** Answer: Simple language, written requirements, change log, aur har sprint chhote demos. Trade-offs ko time, cost aur risk mein explain karta hoon, technical jargon mein nahi.
**Q11. Development lagbhag khatam ho aur requirement change ho jaye to?** Answer: Change likhta hoon, uska impact estimate karta hoon, aur owner se kehta hoon ke choose karein: time barhayen, kuch aur hataein, ya next release mein rakhein. Silently absorb nahi karta.
**Q12. Production mein apni ghalti aur us ke baad kya change hua (aapki story).** Answer: Real example lein: kya toota, kitni jaldi pata chala, sab se pehle kya kiya (damage roka), root cause kya tha, aur kaunsi prevention lagayi (test, check, review rule).

q: H. Web fundamentals aur integration
a:
**Q68. Passenger Rabta app kholta hai aur train search karta hai to kya hota hai?** Answer: App HTTPS request bhejti hai, DNS aur TLS hote hain, load balancer web server ko route karta hai, PHP-FPM Laravel chalata hai, API pehle cache phir database check karti hai, JSON wapas aata hai, aur app render kar deti hai.
**Q69. HTTP methods, idempotency aur status codes.** Answer: GET read, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH partial update, DELETE remove. GET, PUT, DELETE idempotent hain. Codes: 200, 201, 400, 401 (login nahi), 403 (permission nahi), 404, 409, 422, 429, 500, 503.
**Q70. Live train status ke liye REST vs WebSockets vs polling.** Answer: General lookups ke liye caching ke saath REST, live control-room views ke liye WebSockets, aur weak networks ke liye simple short polling fallback.
**Q71. Bahar ke systems (payment, SMS, NADRA, banks) se integrate kaise karte hain?** Answer: Versioned APIs, timeouts, backoff ke saath retries, idempotency keys, signature-checked webhooks, adapter layer, aur har exchange ka log. Main maan kar chalta hoon ke doosri taraf ka system slow ya down ho sakta hai.
**Q72. CORS, cookies, sessions aur tokens.** Answer: CORS browser ka rule hai, authentication nahi. Session server par data rakhta hai aur cookie mein sirf session ID hoti hai. Tokens mobile apps aur APIs ke liye suit karte hain; short expiry plus refresh tokens use karta hoon.
**Q73. Time zones aur languages (English/Urdu).** Answer: Storage UTC mein, display Asia/Karachi mein, Laravel localization, Urdu ke liye right-to-left layout, aur har jagah `utf8mb4`.

q: Honest gaps ke answers (yaad kar lein)
a:
- **Government ya Railways ka experience:** "Directly nahi. Mera experience bade multi-tenant aur high-volume platforms ka hai. Reliability, security, audit trails aur delivery tracking yahan bhi wesey hi matter karte hain, aur main domain rules business team se jaldi seekh leta hoon."
- **Automated testing:** "Main critical flows test aur code review karta hoon, aur automated coverage barha raha hoon. Yahan booking, payment aur permission logic ke liye tests mandatory rakhunga aur CI mein chalaunga."
- **BI tools:** "Maine data side banayi hai. Program jo BI tool use kare, wo seekh loonga."
- **Kubernetes:** "Practically Docker aur Compose, Kubernetes concept level par, aur need ho to seekh loonga."
- **Program details:** "Maine public announcements padhi hain. Main jaanna chahunga ke aaj har module kahan khara hai."

q: T. Big data aur data at scale
a:
**Q133. Big data kya hai, aur kya hamare program ka data "big" hai?** Answer: Big data ka matlab hai volume, velocity aur variety jo ek normal database ya tool aaraam se handle na kar sake. Bahut si trains ke GPS pings, sensor readings aur saalon ki ticket history bari aur fast ho sakti hai. Main hype ke liye "big data" nahi bolunga: pehle measure karunga, phir sab se simple tool choose karunga jo kaam kar de.
**Q134. Storage aur load ka estimate kaise lagate hain?** Answer: Made-up numbers ka example: 2,000 devices har 10 second mein ping karein to 200 pings per second, takreeban 1.7 crore rows roz. Row takreeban 100 bytes ki ho to roz 1.7 GB, saal mein takreeban 630 GB raw, indexes se pehle. Is se pata chalta hai ke partitioning, retention aur summaries pehle din se chahiye. (Real numbers milen to wohi lagayen.)
**Q135. Hot, warm aur cold data kya hain?** Answer: Hot: recent data jo constantly use hota hai (last few days), fast storage par. Warm: pichle kuch mahine, kabhi kabhi query. Cold: law ya audit ke liye purana data, compress karke cheap object storage mein. Retention policy data ko inke beech move karti hai.
**Q136. Downsampling ya roll-up kya hai?** Answer: Raw readings thode time ke liye rakho, phir chhoti summaries store karo: per minute, per hour, per day. Pichle saal ke dashboards daily summaries read karte hain, arbon raw rows nahi.
**Q137. Batch vs stream processing?** Answer: Batch data ko schedule par groups mein process karta hai (raat ki reports). Stream har event ko aate hi process karta hai (live alerts, live map). Operational alerts ke liye streaming, heavy reports ke liye batch.
**Q138. Kaun sa queue ya messaging tool, aur kaise choose karte hain?** Answer: Simple, fast jobs ke liye Redis queues ya Redis Streams. Reliable routing aur acknowledgements ke liye RabbitMQ. Bahut high-volume event streams jinhein kai consumers replay karein, un ke liye Kafka. Honest note: meri hands-on strength Redis queues hain; Kafka concept level par jaanta hoon aur volume ki need se pehle add nahi karunga.
**Q139. Data lake vs data warehouse vs data mart?** Answer: Lake: kai formats mein raw data, cheap storage. Warehouse: cleaned, structured data jo analysis ke liye ho. Mart: ek team ke liye chhota warehouse slice (jaise finance ya operations).
**Q140. Columnar ya OLAP store kya hai, aur kab chahiye?** Answer: Data column ke hisaab se store hota hai, to arbon rows par chand columns read karne wali analytical queries bahut fast hoti hain (ClickHouse ek example hai). Sirf tab consider karunga jab MySQL ki summary tables reports ko fast na rakh saken.
**Q141. GPS pings ke liye MySQL, MongoDB ya time-series database?** Answer: Moderate volume par date partitions wala MySQL achha chalta hai aur ek hi technology rehti hai. MongoDB flexible event documents aur aasan horizontal scaling ke liye. Time-series database built-in retention aur roll-ups deta hai. Main wo choose karunga jo team achhe se operate kar sake, aur latest-position record har soorat mein alag rakhunga.
**Q142. Shard key kya hai, aur hot shard kya hai?** Answer: Shard key decide karti hai ke row kis server par jaye. Bad key (jaise aaj ki date) saare naye writes ek shard par bhej deti hai, jo hot shard ban jata hai. Achhi key load barabar baantti hai, jaise device ID ka hash.
**Q143. CAP theorem aur eventual consistency samjhayen.** Answer: Network split ho to distributed system ko consistency (sab ko wohi data dikhe) aur availability (hamesha jawab de) mein se ek choose karni parti hai. Eventual consistency ka matlab copies thode time ke liye alag ho sakti hain, phir mil jati hain. Live map eventually consistent ho sakta hai; seat booking nahi.
**Q144. Late, duplicate aur out-of-order data kaise handle karte hain?** Answer: Har event ko unique key do (device ID plus timestamp), insert-ignore ya upsert se duplicates harmless, device time aur received time dono store, aur live view tab hi update karo jab event stored value se naya ho.
**Q145. Sensor aur GPS data ki quality kaise achhi rakhte hain?** Answer: Ranges validate (speed, coordinates, fuel level), impossible jumps flag, missing data ko guess nahi karta balki missing mark, raw data ko touch nahi, aur har device ki data-quality percentage report taake kharab devices fix hon.

q: V. Laravel scopes aur Eloquent questions
a:
**Q160. Local scope kya hai?** Answer: Model par reusable query piece, jaise `scopeActive` jo `Ticket::active()->get()` ki tarah chalta hai. Filters ek jagah rehte hain aur code readable hota hai. Naye Laravel versions mein `scope` prefix ke bajaye method par scope attribute bhi lag sakta hai, to team ka version check karein.
**Q161. Global scope kya hai, aur kab use karte hain?** Answer: Aisi scope jo model ki har query par automatically lagti hai, jaise soft deletes, ya tenant ya division filter. Yeh powerful hai kyunke koi bhool nahi sakta, aur yehi iska danger bhi hai.
**Q162. Global scopes ke dangers kya hain?** Answer: Inhein `withoutGlobalScopes()` se bypass kiya ja sakta hai, `DB::table()` ya raw SQL par apply nahi hoti, joins aur relationship queries mein surprise de sakti hain, queue jobs aur console commands mein (jahan logged-in user nahi) alag behave karti hain, aur logic reader se chhupa deti hain. Main aise tests likhta hoon jo prove karein ke user doosri division ka data read nahi kar sakta.
**Q163. Division scoping ka example dikhayen.** Answer: `DivisionScope` normal staff ke liye `where('division_id', auth()->user()->division_id)` lagata hai, aur headquarters roles ise skip kar dete hain. Jobs mein main `auth()` par rely nahi karta, division explicitly pass karta hoon.
**Q164. Scopes vs repository vs query object?** Answer: Chhote reusable filters ke liye scopes. Complex, multi-step ya cross-model queries aur reporting ke liye query objects ya repositories. Jo layers chahiye nahi, wo add nahi karta.
**Q165. `whereHas` vs join: kaun sa fast hai?** Answer: `whereHas` subquery use karta hai aur clear hai, lekin bari tables par achhe indexes ke saath join ya `whereExists` fast ho sakta hai. Main EXPLAIN se measure karke choose karta hoon.
**Q166. Loop ke andar update karne par `chunk()` rows kyun skip ya repeat kar sakta hai?** Answer: Agar chunking ke dauran filter ya ordering wala column change ho jaye to offset boundaries shift ho jati hain. Updates ke liye `chunkById()` (ya `lazyById()`) use karein kyunke yeh primary key se pages banata hai.
**Q167. Kya `firstOrCreate` ya `updateOrCreate` concurrency mein safe hain?** Answer: Khud nahi. Do requests dono kuch nahi paa kar dono insert kar sakti hain. Unique constraint lagayen, duplicate-key error handle karein, ya `upsert` use karein. Uniqueness database ko enforce karni chahiye.
**Q168. Transaction ke andar job dispatch hui aur record nahi mila. Kyun?** Answer: Worker transaction commit hone se pehle start ho gaya. Commit ke baad dispatch karein (`afterCommit`, ya `after_commit` queue setting) taake job chalne tak data maujood ho.
**Q169. Bulk update par mera observer kyun nahi chala?** Answer: Query builder se mass updates aur deletes model events skip kar dete hain kyunke koi model instance load nahi hota. Jahan events zaroori hon wahan model-level updates use karein, ya audit step explicitly likhein.
**Q170. Lazy-loading aur doosri Eloquent mistakes jaldi kaise pakadte hain?** Answer: Non-production mein `Model::preventLazyLoading()` aur strict mode, jo lazy loading, missing attributes aur silently discard hui fills par error deta hai. Is se N+1 problems tests mein visible failures ban jati hain.
**Q171. Karoron rows fast kaise insert karte hain?** Answer: Chand hazar ke batches mein bulk `insert()` ya `upsert()`, har batch ke liye ek transaction, kam indexes, aur queued job se. Loop mein `create()` slow hai kyunke events aur har row ki ek query hoti hai.
**Q172. Counter ko safely kaise barhate hain?** Answer: `increment()` atomic `UPDATE ... SET count = count + 1` chalata hai. Read karke PHP mein add karke save karna concurrency mein lost updates deta hai.

q: X. Tricky aur "lines ke beech" wale questions
a:
Yeh questions simple lagte hain, lekin interviewer honesty, judgement, ethics ya attitude check kar raha hota hai. Har question ke saath likha hai ke asal mein kya parakha ja raha hai.
**Q173. "Aap coding prefer karte hain ya team manage karna?"** Parakh: kya aap delivery-owner role ke liye dono kar sakte hain. Answer: "Mujhe dono pasand hain. Mushkil hisson par khud code karta hoon aur quality high rakhta hoon, aur planning, review aur blockers hata kar team ko lead karta hoon."
**Q174. "Ek senior officer kehta hai database mein seedha data change kar do, koi record nahi chahiye."** Parakh: integrity aur ethics. Answer: "Main silently data edit nahi karunga. Written request maangunga, controlled aur logged correction approval ke saath karunga, aur samjhaunga ke audit trail sab ko protect karta hai, us officer ko bhi."
**Q175. "Ek dost kisi ka ticket ya personal record dekhne ko kehta hai."** Parakh: data ethics. Answer: "Nahi. Access sirf kaam ke purpose ke liye hai aur har view log hota hai. Main official channel suggest karunga."
**Q176. "Minister ke demo se pehle bug mila. Kya aap batayenge?"** Parakh: pressure mein honesty. Answer: "Ji haan, apne manager ko foran, risk aur safe plan ke saath: fix karein, us path se bachein, ya jo stable hai wo dikhayen. Main chhupaunga nahi."
**Q177. "Hamari list ka ek tool aap nahi jaante. Kya phir bhi kaam kar sakte hain?"** Parakh: honesty aur learning speed. Answer: "Maine isay professionally use nahi kiya. Sab se close cheez jo maine ki wo yeh hai, aur main isay pehle haftaon mein is tareeqe se seekhunga." Aisi skill ka claim kabhi na karein jo aap explain na kar sakein.
**Q178. "Aap ka sab se weak area kya hai?"** Parakh: self-awareness. Answer: Real aur fixable weakness chunein: automated test coverage, ya BI tools, ya Kubernetes depth. Batayen ke us par kya kar rahe hain. "Main bahut mehnat karta hoon" jaise jawab se bachein.
**Q179. "Aap ka experience zyada private sector ka hai. Government ka kaam slow aur bureaucratic hota hai. Kya yeh problem hai?"** Parakh: adaptability. Answer: "Approvals aur documentation accountability ke liye hote hain. Main inhein pehle se plan karta hoon, written record rakhta hoon, aur sign-off ka wait karte hue kaam parallel chalata rehta hoon."
**Q180. "Aap PITB ke technical decision se agree nahi karte. Kya karenge?"** Parakh: professional disagreement. Answer: "Main data ke saath (risk, cost, examples) pehle private mein baat uthata hoon, ek alternative propose karta hoon, aur final decision accept karta hoon. Decision hone ke baad poori tarah support karta hoon aur jo risks bataye thay un par nazar rakhta hoon."
**Q181. "Vendor ka code poor quality hai aur aap ko us se integrate karna hai."** Parakh: pragmatism. Answer: "Main usay adapter mein wrap karta hoon, jis behavior par depend karta hoon uske gird tests lagata hoon, sab kuch log karta hoon, vendor ko defects written mein report karta hoon, aur unke problems apne code mein nahi laata."
**Q182. "Aap apni current company kyun chhor rahe hain?"** Parakh: attitude aur stability. Answer: Aap ka apna honest jawab. Positive aur forward-looking rakhein: scale, ownership aur national system banane ka moqa. Apne employer ki burai na karein.
**Q183. "Yeh contract hai. Aap ki salary expectation kya hai?"** Parakh: realism. Answer: Pehle se senior engineers aur contract grade ki market range research karein, reasonable range batayen, aur kahein ke sahi scope ke liye flexible hain. Aise numbers na batayen jinka defence na kar sakein.
**Q184. "Kya aap ke CV mein koi cheez hai jo aap detail mein explain nahi kar sakte?"** Parakh: CV honesty. Answer: Interview se pehle CV ki har line explain karne ke liye ready rahein. Agar kuch thin ho to seedha kahein: "Maine isay project ke ek hisse mein use kiya, zyada tar X."
**Q185. "Aap ko long hours kaam karna hoga aur raat ko urgent tasks aa sakte hain. Theek hai?"** Parakh: operations commitment. Answer: "Main samajhta hoon IT operations mein incidents hote hain. Main clear on-call rules aur achhi monitoring prefer karta hoon taake raat ka kaam kam ho, aur jab ho to properly respond karta hoon."
**Q186. "Aap pehle 30 dinon mein kya karenge?"** Parakh: planning. Answer: Architecture aur data flows seekhunga, owners se milunga, incident history padhunga, local environment set karunga, top teen risks (testing, monitoring, deployments) dhoondunga, aur ek chhoti safe improvement deliver karunga.

q: Z3. Networking aur infrastructure basics (fiber backbone wala pehlu)
a:
**Q202. DNS simple words mein.** Answer: Yeh naam ko IP address mein convert karta hai. A record naam ko IPv4 address se jorta hai, CNAME alias hai, aur TTL batata hai ke answer kitni der cache rahe. Server move se pehle TTL kam karta hoon.
**Q203. TCP vs UDP?** Answer: TCP reliable aur ordered hai (web, databases). UDP lightweight hai aur koi guarantee nahi (kuch tracking devices aur streaming). Bahut se GPS devices TCP ya UDP use karte hain, to ingestion service ko lost ya duplicate packets handle karne chahiye.
**Q204. Devices ke liye MQTT vs HTTP?** Answer: MQTT lightweight publish/subscribe protocol hai jo bahut se chhote devices aur weak networks ke liye suit karta hai. HTTP simple hai aur har jagah chalta hai. Hazaron devices jo chhote, frequent messages bhejein un ke liye MQTT attractive hai; main choice is par karunga ke devices kya support karte hain.
**Q205. Firewall, NAT, VPN, private network?** Answer: Firewall rule ke hisaab se traffic allow ya block karta hai. NAT bahut si private machines ko ek public address share karne deta hai. VPN private network mein secure tunnel deta hai. Databases aur internal services private network par rehti hain, public address ke baghair.
**Q206. Layer 4 vs layer 7 load balancer?** Answer: Layer 4 IP aur port se route karta hai (fast, simple). Layer 7 HTTP samajhta hai, to path se route, TLS terminate aur application health check kar sakta hai. Web apps ke liye aam tor par layer 7.
**Q207. Latency vs bandwidth vs throughput?** Answer: Latency ek message ki delay hai. Bandwidth link ki maximum capacity hai. Throughput actual deliver hone wali miqdar hai. Bara link bhi slow lag sakta hai agar latency zyada ho.
**Q208. Production mein TLS certificate expire ho gaya. Ab kya, aur kaise rokein?** Answer: Foran renew aur deploy, phir verify. Rokne ke liye: automatic renewal, expiry monitoring jis ka alert hafton pehle aaye, aur har certificate ka ek owner.

q: Z4. Redis aur caching practice mein
a:
**Q209. Redis ke kaun se data structures use karte hain, aur kis liye?** Answer: Cache aur counters ke liye strings, objects ke liye hashes (har train ki latest position), queues ke liye lists aur streams, unique members ke liye sets, rankings aur delayed items ke liye sorted sets, aur locks aur rate limits ke liye expiry wali keys.
**Q210. Redis persistence: RDB vs AOF?** Answer: RDB periodic snapshots leta hai (fast restart, recent writes lose ho sakti hain). AOF har write log karta hai (kam loss, bari files). Agar Redis sirf cache rakhe to persistence ki zaroorat nahi. Agar queues rakhe to AOF on karta hoon aur failure ka plan rakhta hoon.
**Q211. Redis ki memory full ho jaye to kya hota hai?** Answer: Wo eviction policy follow karta hai: cache ke liye LRU-style policy purani keys hata deti hai. Queues ya locks ke liye eviction dangerous hai, to alag Redis instance bina eviction ke rakhta hoon aur memory alerts lagata hoon.
**Q212. Kya Redis locks safe hain?** Answer: Expiry wala simple lock bahut kaamon ke liye theek hai, lekin fail ho sakta hai agar kaam jaari rahe aur lock expire ho jaye, ya Redis failover ho. Paison ya seats ke liye main kabhi sirf cache lock par rely nahi karta: database constraint final protection hai.
**Q213. Redis single point of failure hai. Kya karenge?** Answer: Automatic failover ke liye Sentinel ke saath replication, ya sharding ke liye Redis Cluster, aur app ko cache outage survive karne ke qabil banao (database par fallback aur slow ho, crash na ho).

q: Z9. Live coding aur logic tasks (paper par practice)
Poora raasta ek nazar mein
a:
```
Client -> DNS -> TCP/TLS -> (CDN / load balancer) -> Nginx
      -> FastCGI (unix socket ya 127.0.0.1:9000) -> PHP-FPM master
      -> idle FPM worker -> public/index.php -> Laravel -> response
      -> wapas FPM -> Nginx -> client
```
**S1. \[Senior\] Aap ka server request ko Laravel ke index file tak pohanchne se pehle kaise process karta hai?** Answer: Pehle client DNS se IP leta hai aur TCP connection plus TLS handshake hota hai (aksar load balancer ya CDN par terminate). Phir request Nginx tak aati hai. Nginx server block aur `location` match karta hai. Static files (CSS, JS, images) wo seedha khud serve kar deta hai. PHP requests ke liye `try_files` unhein `index.php` par bhejta hai aur `fastcgi_pass` se FastCGI protocol mein PHP-FPM ko deta hai (unix socket ya TCP). FPM ka master process pool se ek idle worker ko request assign karta hai, worker `public/index.php` chalata hai, Laravel boot hota hai, response wapas Nginx ke raste client tak jata hai. *Cross-question: Static files Laravel tak kyun nahi jatin?* Answer: Nginx bahut fast hai static serve karne mein aur PHP worker ko block nahi karta. Isi liye static files ko CDN ya Nginx se serve karna PHP workers bachata hai.
**S2. \[Mid\] FPM kya hai?** Answer: PHP-FPM ka matlab FastCGI Process Manager. Ek master process hota hai jo workers ka pool manage karta hai. Har worker ek time par sirf ek request handle karta hai (threads nahi). Master workers ko spawn, kill aur recycle karta hai. Important settings:
- `pm = static`: workers ki fixed tadaad, predictable, high-traffic ke liye achha.
- `pm = dynamic`: `pm.max_children`, `pm.start_servers`, `pm.min_spare_servers`, `pm.max_spare_servers` ke beech workers ghat-barhte hain.
- `pm = ondemand`: jab request aaye tab worker banta hai, kam traffic wali sites ke liye.
- `pm.max_requests`: worker itni requests ke baad restart hota hai (memory leaks se bachne ke liye).
- `request_terminate_timeout` aur `slowlog`: atki hui requests ko pakadne ke liye.
**S3. \[Senior\] Nginx concurrent requests ko FPM workers tak kaise pohanchata hai?** Answer: Nginx event-driven hai (Linux par epoll). Ek Nginx worker process hazaron connections non-blocking tareeqe se sambhal sakta hai, kyunke wo wait nahi karta, events par react karta hai (`worker_processes auto`, `worker_connections`). PHP request ke liye wo FPM se connection kholta hai (`fastcgi_pass`, chaho to `fastcgi_keep_conn` se connection reuse). FPM ka socket requests accept karta hai aur master unhein idle workers ko deta hai. Nginx PHP ki parwah nahi karta: wo bas FPM ke jawab ka intezar karta hai. To bottleneck aksar Nginx nahi, FPM workers ki tadaad hoti hai.
**S4. \[Senior\] Aap ka PHP server ek waqt mein kitni requests process kar sakta hai?** Answer: Ek FPM pool mein concurrent requests ki limit `pm.max_children` hai: har worker ek request. Lekin asal sawal yeh hai ke sahi number kitna ho:
- **Memory limit:** `max_children` taqreeban (PHP ke liye available RAM) / (har worker ki average memory). Misaal: 4 GB PHP ke liye aur har worker 50 MB, to taqreeban 80 workers.
- **CPU:** CPU-heavy kaam mein cores se zyada workers faida nahi dete. Jo requests zyada waqt database ya API ka wait karti hain wahan cores se zyada workers chal sakte hain.
- **Database connections:** har worker ek DB connection pakad sakta hai, to `max_connections` bhi dekhna parta hai.
- **Throughput ka formula:** requests per second taqreeban = workers / average response time. 80 workers aur 200 ms response se takreeban 400 req/s. Agar response 2 second ho jaye to wohi 80 workers sirf takreeban 40 req/s dete hain. Isi liye slow requests system ko maar deti hain. *Cross-question: Kya threads se behtar ho sakta hai?* Answer: FPM mein threads nahi. Laravel Octane (Swoole ya RoadRunner) app ko memory mein zinda rakhta hai aur concurrency alag tarah handle karta hai, lekin us mein memory leaks aur global state ka khayal rakhna parta hai.
**S5. \[Senior\] Jo requests process nahi ho rahi, unka kya hota hai? Woh kahan hold hoti hain?** Answer: Agar saare workers busy hon to nayi connections FPM socket ki **listen queue (backlog)** mein kernel ke paas intezar karti hain. Backlog ki size `listen.backlog` aur OS ki `net.core.somaxconn` se tay hoti hai (default aksar 511, apne config mein check karein). Phir:
- Agar worker thodi der mein free ho jaye, request chal padti hai, lekin user ko slow response milta hai.
- Agar Nginx FPM ka jawab `fastcgi_read_timeout` tak na paaye, user ko **504 Gateway Timeout** milta hai.
- Agar backlog full ho jaye ya FPM down ho, to Nginx ko connection nahi milta aur wo **502 Bad Gateway** deta hai.
- FPM log mein warning aati hai: `server reached pm.max_children setting`. Yeh sab se pehla signal hai.
*Fix ka tareeqa:* pehle slow cause dhoondo (slow query, slow external API), slow kaam queue mein bhejo, caching lagao, timeouts sahi rakho, `max_children` RAM ke hisaab se tune karo, rate limiting aur load balancer ke peeche zyada servers lagao, aur monitoring mein "active workers", "listen queue" aur 502/504 par alerts rakho. Sirf `max_children` barhana aksar masla nahi hal karta; yeh RAM khatam kar ke server ko aur girata hai.
**Quick tuning checklist (yaad rakhne ke liye):** OPcache on, `config:cache` aur `route:cache` aur `view:cache`, `pm.max_requests` set, `request_terminate_timeout` set, slowlog on, Nginx `keepalive` aur gzip, static files CDN par, sessions aur cache Redis mein, heavy kaam queue mein.
# Part 2: Top 25 PHP & Laravel questions (jawab ke saath)
p: Senior PHP Laravel Interview 5 Server Questions   Top 25 (Roman Urdu Answers)

q: PHP Core aur OOP
a:
**Q1. \[Mid\] PHP 8.x aur purane versions ka kya farq hai?** Answer: PHP 8.0 mein JIT, union types, named arguments, attributes, `match`, constructor promotion aur nullsafe operator aaye. 8.1 mein enums, readonly properties, fibers, never type. 8.2 mein readonly classes aur DNF types. 8.3 mein typed class constants aur `#[Override]`. 8.4 mein property hooks aur asymmetric visibility. Practical faida: ghaltiyan compile ya type level par pakri jati hain, code short aur clear hota hai, aur performance behtar. Main jo features asal mein use karta hoon wohi batata hoon: enums, readonly, match, constructor promotion.
**Q2. \[Mid\] SOLID principles real PHP example ke saath samjhayen.** Answer: **S**: ek class ka ek kaam, jaise `TicketPriceCalculator` sirf price nikale, SMS na bheje. **O**: naya feature code add karke, purana edit karke nahi: nayi `SmsChannel` class add ho, `NotificationService` na badle. **L**: child class parent ki jagah chal jaye bina behavior toote. **I**: chhoti interfaces, `Printable` aur `Exportable` alag. **D**: high-level class concrete par nahi, interface par depend kare: `BookingService` ko `PaymentGateway` interface mile, `StripeGateway` nahi.
**Q3. \[Mid\] Interface, abstract class aur trait ka farq?** Answer: Interface sirf contract hai (kya karna hai). Abstract class mein shared code aur kuch abstract methods ho sakte hain aur ek hi class extend hoti hai. Trait reusable code hai jo kai classes mein mix ho sakta hai, lekin us ka koi type nahi. Main provider-swap wali cheezon ke liye interface, shared base behavior ke liye abstract class, aur chhote reusable helpers (jaise logging) ke liye trait use karta hoon.
**Q4. \[Mid\] Dependency injection aur Dependency Inversion Principle PHP mein kaise kaam karte hain?** Answer: DIP kehta hai: high-level code abstraction par depend kare, concrete class par nahi. DI us ka tareeqa hai: class ko dependency constructor se milti hai. Laravel mein container interface ko implementation se bind karta hai: `$this->app->bind(SmsGateway::class, TwilioGateway::class)`. Faida: test mein fake inject kar sakte hain aur provider badalna aasan hai.
**Q5. \[Senior\] PHP memory management, garbage collection aur common memory leak scenarios.** Answer: PHP reference counting use karta hai: jab value ka koi reference na bache to memory free. Circular references ke liye cycle garbage collector chalta hai (`gc_collect_cycles()`). Normal web request mein memory request ke saath khatam ho jati hai (shared-nothing), isliye leaks aam tor par long-running processes mein dikhte hain: queue workers, Octane, scheduler commands. Common causes: bade Eloquent collections ko loop mein load karna, static arrays ya singletons mein data jama hona, listeners ka jama hona, unbounded in-memory cache, closures jo bade objects pakre rahein. Fixes: `chunkById`/`lazyById`, `unset`, `queue:work --max-jobs --max-time --memory` se worker ko restart, `pm.max_requests` FPM mein, aur memory usage ko monitor karna.

q: Laravel Framework
a:
**Q6. \[Mid\] Laravel request lifecycle samjhayen.** Answer: `public/index.php` autoloader load karta hai aur application bootstrap karta hai, HTTP kernel request leta hai, service providers register aur boot hote hain, global middleware chalti hai, router route match karta hai, route middleware, controller, response banta hai, aur wapas middleware se guzar kar client ko jata hai. Aakhir mein terminable middleware chalti hai. Senior follow-up: isi liye bootstrap ka kaam ko cache karte hain (`config:cache`, `route:cache`).
**Q7. \[Mid\] Service Container kya hai aur dependency injection kaise kaam karta hai?** Answer: Container Laravel ka IoC container hai jo classes banata hai aur unki dependencies khud resolve karta hai (reflection se type-hints dekh kar). `bind` har baar nayi instance deta hai, `singleton` ek hi instance, `scoped` request ya job ke dauran ek instance. Contextual binding se alag classes ko alag implementation de sakte hain. Example: controller ke constructor mein `BookingService` type-hint karo, container usay khud bana ke inject kar dega.
**Q8. \[Mid\] Service Providers aur Facades mein kya farq hai?** Answer: Service Provider app ko bootstrap karta hai: `register()` mein bindings, `boot()` mein jab sab ready ho to kaam (routes, observers, macros). Facade static-jaisi syntax hai (`Cache::get(...)`) jo asal mein container se resolve hui instance par method forward karti hai (`getFacadeAccessor`). Testing mein `Cache::shouldReceive()` ya `Mail::fake()` use hota hai. Mera view: business classes mein constructor injection prefer karta hoon, facades zyada tar framework helpers ke liye.
**Q9. \[Mid\] Middleware kya hai aur custom middleware kaise banate hain?** Answer: Middleware request ke aage peeche ka layer hai (pipeline): auth, rate limit, logging, headers. Banane ke liye `php artisan make:middleware EnsureDivisionHeader`, phir `handle($request, Closure $next)` mein check karke `return $next($request)` ya error response. Register: route par alias, ya group mein, ya global. Parameters ke saath bhi chal sakti hai (`role:admin`). Response ke baad kaam ke liye terminable middleware.
**Q10. \[Mid\] Events, Listeners, Jobs aur Queues mein kya farq hai?** Answer: **Event**: "kuch ho gaya" (`TicketPaid`), decoupled notification. **Listener**: us event par react karta hai, chaho to `ShouldQueue` se background mein. **Job**: ek explicit kaam jo aap queue mein dispatch karte hain (`SendTicketSms::dispatch($id)`). **Queue**: transport aur storage (Redis, database, SQS) jahan jobs wait karte hain, aur workers unhein process karte hain. Sawal yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: event batata hai kya hua, job batata hai kya karna hai, queue batati hai kahan wait karna hai.
**Q11. \[Mid\] Authentication vs authorization, Guards aur Policies.** Answer: Authentication matlab "aap kaun hain" (login). Authorization matlab "aap kya kar sakte hain". Guards define karte hain ke user kaise authenticate ho (session guard web ke liye, Sanctum token API aur SPA ke liye, Passport OAuth ke liye). Authorization ke liye Gates (simple checks) aur Policies (model ke hisaab se rules: `update`, `delete`). Controller mein `$this->authorize('update', $inspection)`. Senior point: har record par ownership aur division check, warna IDOR.
**Q12. \[Mid\] Eloquent ORM vs Query Builder.** Answer: Eloquent model, relationships, events, casts, accessors aur soft deletes deta hai, readable hai, lekin har row ka model hydrate hona memory aur CPU leta hai. Query Builder fluent SQL hai jo seedha rows (stdClass) deta hai, fast hai, bulk aur reporting ke liye behtar. Main normal CRUD aur business logic ke liye Eloquent, heavy reports, bulk updates aur aggregations ke liye Query Builder ya raw SQL use karta hoon. Eloquent par `->toBase()` ya `DB::table()` se hydration bacha sakte hain.
**Q13. \[Mid\] Laravel mein N+1 problem kaise rokte hain?** Answer: Eager loading: `Ticket::with('train', 'station')->get()`, count ke liye `withCount()`, bad mein zaroorat ho to `$tickets->load('train')`. Constrained eager loading: `with(['pings' => fn ($q) => $q->latest()->limit(1)])` ya `latestOfMany`. Development mein `Model::preventLazyLoading()` lagata hoon taake N+1 error ban jaye, aur Debugbar ya Telescope se query count dekhta hoon.
**Q14. \[Senior\] Database transactions aur failures kaise handle karte hain?** Answer: `DB::transaction(function () { ... }, 3)`: exception aaye to automatic rollback, aur doosra parameter deadlock par retry attempts. Manual control ke liye `beginTransaction`, `commit`, `rollBack`. Nested transactions savepoints use karti hain. Senior points: (1) transaction short rakho, (2) transaction ke andar external calls (SMS, payment API) mat karo kyunke wo rollback nahi hoti, (3) jobs aur events `afterCommit` dispatch karo, (4) failure par log aur compensating action (jaise refund ya release) rakho.
**Q15. \[Mid\] Redis ke saath caching kaise implement karte hain?** Answer: `.env` mein cache store Redis, phir `Cache::remember('train:7:latest', 30, fn () => Ping::latestFor(7))`. Tags (Redis par supported), `Cache::lock()` se atomic locks, aur write par key clear. Senior points: cache stampede se bachne ke liye lock ya jitter wali expiry, har key ka scope clear (user-specific data ko shared key mein nahi), seat jaise critical data par bohat short TTL aur final database check, aur Redis memory eviction policy cache aur queues ke liye alag.

q: **Infra:** FPM workers ka size, keepalive, replicas. Har fix ke baad dobara measure, aur result ka number batao ("8 second se 400 ms").
a:
**Q17. \[Mid\] Database indexes performance kaise behtar karte hain, aur kab nuksan dete hain?** Answer: Index lookup, filter, join aur sort tez karte hain (B-tree se poori table scan nahi). Nuksan: har INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ke saath index bhi update hota hai (write slow), storage barhta hai, bahut zyada ya low-cardinality indexes optimizer ko confuse ya waste karte hain, aur function lagane (`WHERE DATE(created_at) = ...`) ya `LIKE '%x'` par index use nahi hota. Composite index mein leftmost-prefix rule.
**Q18. \[Senior\] Laravel mein millions of records efficiently kaise process karte hain?** Answer: Pehle sochta hoon kya ye set-based SQL mein ho sakta hai (ek `UPDATE ... WHERE` poori table par database khud karega). Agar PHP mein chahiye to `chunkById()` ya `lazyById()` se rows batches mein, ya `Bus::batch()` se jobs mein todna taake parallel workers chalein. Inserts `insert()` ya `upsert()` batches mein. Exports stream karo (`response()->streamDownload`, `fputcsv`) aur memory monitor. Eloquent models ki jagah ho sake to Query Builder, kyunke model hydration mehnga hai.
**Q19. \[Senior\] `chunk()`, `chunkById()`, `lazy()` aur `cursor()` mein farq?** Answer:
- **`chunk(n)`:** offset par based queries, har batch ke liye ek query. Agar loop ke andar filter ya order wala column update karo to rows skip ya repeat ho sakti hain.
- **`chunkById(n)`:** primary key par based (`WHERE id > last`), updates ke liye safe aur fast.
- **`lazy()`:** chunks mein query karta hai lekin aap ko ek ek model ka LazyCollection deta hai, to code seedha lagta hai aur memory chunk-size jitni. Updates ke liye `lazyById()`.
- **`cursor()`:** ek hi query, ek ek model hydrate hota hai (generator), PHP-side models ki memory kam. Lekin result set driver level par buffer ho sakta hai (MySQL buffered queries), connection lambi der khula rehta hai, aur eager loading nahi chalti. Meri rule of thumb: updates ho to `chunkById`/`lazyById`, sirf padhna ho aur relations chahiye to `lazy()`, bahut simple stream ho to `cursor()` (aur result size ka dhyan).
**Q20. \[Mid\] Slow SQL queries kaise debug karte hain aur execution plan kaise analyze karte hain?** Answer: Slow query log ya Laravel Pulse/Telescope se slow queries pakadta hoon (`DB::listen` bhi). Phir `EXPLAIN` (MySQL 8 mein `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` asal timing bhi deta hai): `type` (ALL matlab full scan), `key`, `rows`, aur `Extra` mein filesort ya temporary. Fix: sahi composite index, query rewrite, kam columns, summary table. Phir dobara EXPLAIN aur real timing compare.

q: Architecture, security aur scalability
a:
**Q21. \[Senior\] Scalable REST API Laravel mein kaise design karenge?** Answer: Stateless API (Sanctum tokens), resource-based URLs, versioning (`/api/v1`), pagination aur filtering har list par, consistent error format, rate limiting, idempotency keys POST ke liye, ETag ya cache headers, slow kaam queue mein, caching Redis mein, aur load balancer ke peeche zyada app servers. Database side par indexes, read replicas heavy reads ke liye, aur monitoring (error rate, latency percentiles, queue length). Scale ke liye pehle bottleneck measure karta hoon, phir upar se infra barhata hoon.
**Q22. \[Senior\] Repository Pattern, Service Layer, DTOs: kab kaunsa useful hai?** Answer: **Service layer:** business logic ek jagah (booking ka flow), controllers patle. Zyada tar projects mein yeh sab se zyada kaam ka hai. **Repository:** jab queries complex ya reused hon, ya data source badalne ka imkan ho, warna Eloquent khud kaafi hai aur extra layer sirf boilerplate. **DTO:** jab data layers ke beech clear shape mein jata ho (API request se service tak, ya external vendor ka response), type-safe aur validated, arrays se behtar. Rule: layer tab add karo jab us ka masla saamne ho, pehle se nahi.
**Q23. \[Mid\] SQL injection, CSRF, XSS aur mass-assignment se kaise bachte hain?** Answer:
- **SQL injection:** Eloquent aur Query Builder bindings use karte hain; raw queries mein `?` placeholders; user se aaye column ya order by ki whitelist.
- **CSRF:** web forms mein `@csrf` token, `SameSite` cookies; token-based APIs mein CSRF ki zaroorat nahi par token safe rakho.
- **XSS:** Blade ka `{{ }}` output escape karta hai; `{!! !!}` sirf trusted content par; user HTML ko sanitize karo; CSP header.
- **Mass assignment:** `$fillable`, aur `$request->validated()` hi use karo, `$request->all()` nahi.
**Q24. \[Senior\] Retries, timeouts aur failed-job handling wala queue-based system kaise design karenge?** Answer: Job class mein `$tries`, `$backoff = [10, 60, 300]`, `$timeout`, aur `retryUntil()` jab time ke hisaab se retry chahiye. Job idempotent ho (dobara chale to double effect nahi). `failed(Throwable $e)` method mein alert ya compensating action, aur `failed_jobs` table se `php artisan queue:retry`. Control: `WithoutOverlapping`, `RateLimited` middleware, `ShouldBeUnique`, chains aur `Bus::batch()` jab jobs ka silsila ho. Dhyan rakhne ki baat: `retry_after` (queue config) `timeout` se bara hona chahiye, warna ek job do workers ko mil jata hai. Workers ko Horizon ya Supervisor se chalayen, `queue:work --max-jobs --max-time` se recycle, aur queue length aur failed jobs par alerts.
**Q25. \[Senior\] Bari Laravel application ko modular architecture ya microservices mein kaise structure karenge?** Answer: Main pehle **modular monolith** chunta hoon: ek codebase aur ek deploy, lekin clear modules (Ticketing, Tracking, Inspection, Reporting), har ek ke apne routes, models, services, policies aur tests. Modules ek doosre ke internals ko direct touch nahi karte; interfaces ya events se baat karte hain. Microservices tab jab ek hissa alag scale ho (jaise GPS ingestion), alag team ownership ho, ya alag technology chahiye. Microservices ki cost: network failures, distributed transactions, deployment aur monitoring ka overhead. Isi liye pehle boundaries saaf karta hoon, phir zaroorat par ek module ko service banata hoon.

q: `cursor()`: ek query, ek ek row
a:
```php
foreach (Ticket::where('status', 'paid')->cursor() as $ticket) { /* ... */ }
```
Ek hi `select` chalta hai aur Laravel PDO se row ba row fetch kar ke ek ek model banata hai (generator). PHP mein hydrated models ka sirf ek hota hai. Lekin teen gotchas:
- MySQL ka PDO default **buffered query** use karta hai, yani driver poora result set pehle PHP memory mein la deta hai (raw rows, models nahi). Phir bhi bade tables par memory badh sakti hai. Unbuffered karne ke liye `config/database.php` ke `options` mein `PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY => false`; phir ek connection par result poora parhne se pehle doosri query nahi chal sakti (error "unbuffered queries are active").
- Connection aur statement poore loop tak khule rehte hain, to lambi loop mein timeouts aur locks ka khatra.
- **Eager loading nahi hoti**, to loop mein relation access karoge to N+1 ban jata hai.
### Comparison
| Method | Queries | Memory (PHP) | Update safe? | Eager loading | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chunk(n)` | ek per batch, OFFSET | n models | Nahi (rows skip) | Haan | bade offset slow |
| `chunkById(n)` | ek per batch, `id >` | n models | Haan | Haan | sab se safe aur fast |
| `lazy(n)` | `chunk` jaisi | n models | Nahi | Haan | simple LazyCollection API |
| `lazyById(n)` | `chunkById` jaisi | n models | Haan | Haan | updates ke liye `lazy` ka version |
| `cursor()` | ek query | 1 model, lekin driver buffer | Dhyan se | Nahi | connection lambi khuli |
**Interview line:** "Updates ho to `chunkById`/`lazyById`, kyunke keyset pagination rows skip nahi karti aur index par chalti hai. `chunk` offset par chalta hai aur filter badalne par rows chhor deta hai. `cursor` ek query stream karta hai lekin driver buffering aur eager loading ki limit hai."
Bonus: bade batch jobs mein sab se achha pattern: `chunkById` se ids ke chhote batches banao aur har batch ko queue job (`Bus::batch`) mein bhej do, taake workers parallel chalein aur ek job ki nakami baqi ko na roke.

Facade ek **static-jaisi syntax wala proxy** hai jo asal mein container ke ek object ko call karta hai. Us mein business logic nahi hoti. Isliye "facade matlab static class" kehna galat hai: `Cache::get('k')` kisi static method ko nahi, ek zinda instance ko call karta hai.
In Laravel, a **Facade** is a class that provides a **"static" interface to services registered inside the application's Service Container**. \[[1](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/5.2/facades), [2](https://dev.to/anashussain284/laravel-facades-explained-why-they-feel-so-clean-and-powerful-1ldj)\]

They dynamically resolve real, instanced objects out of the container behind the scenes and pass your calls to them. \[[1](https://masteryoflaravel.medium.com/the-facade-pattern-in-laravel-a-comprehensive-guide-2a9619e79375), [2](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/5.2/facades), [3](https://dev.to/anashussain284/laravel-facades-explained-why-they-feel-so-clean-and-powerful-1ldj)\]

q: `bind` vs `singleton` vs `scoped` vs `instance`
a:
```php
$this->app->bind(Counter::class, fn () => new Counter);
app(Counter::class) === app(Counter::class);   // false: har baar nayi instance
$this->app->singleton(Counter::class, fn () => new Counter);
app(Counter::class) === app(Counter::class);   // true: ek hi instance
```
| Method | Lifetime | Kab |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bind` | har resolve par nayi instance | chhote stateful objects, jinhein har baar fresh chahiye |
| `singleton` | application ke lifetime tak ek instance | mehngi to banne wali, stateless ya shared cheez (API client, config reader) |
| `scoped` | ek request ya job ke dauran ek instance, phir saaf | naye versions mein request-specific state (current division, tenant) |
| `instance` | aap ka bana banaya object register | tests mein fake, ya pehle se bana hua object |
**Bara gotcha:** PHP-FPM mein har request ke baad process ki memory saaf, to singleton bhi request tak hi zinda. Lekin **queue workers aur Octane** mein process lamba chalta hai, to singleton mein rakhi hui user, tenant ya request ki state agle job ya request mein leak hoti hai (data ek user ka doosre ko dikhna, security bug). Aise objects ke liye `scoped`, ya state ko object mein rakhne ke bajaye method ke parameter mein dein.

q: Deep dive 7: Joins
a:
Join do (ya zyada) tables ki rows ko ek condition (`ON`) par jorta hai. Normalized database mein data alag tables mein hota hai (trains alag, tickets alag), aur report ke liye unhein jorna parta hai.
### Types
```sql
-- INNER JOIN: sirf wo rows jahan dono taraf match mile
SELECT t.name, k.id, k.amount
FROM trains t
INNER JOIN tickets k ON k.train_id = t.id;
-- LEFT JOIN: left table ki SAARI rows; match na ho to right ke columns NULL
SELECT t.name, k.id
FROM trains t
LEFT JOIN tickets k ON k.train_id = t.id;
-- Anti-join: wo trains jin ka ek bhi ticket nahi
SELECT t.*
FROM trains t
LEFT JOIN tickets k ON k.train_id = t.id
WHERE k.id IS NULL;                       -- ya NOT EXISTS (subquery)
-- RIGHT JOIN: LEFT ka ulta (aksar tables ulta kar ke LEFT hi likhte hain)
-- FULL OUTER JOIN: MySQL mein nahi; LEFT aur RIGHT ka UNION
SELECT ... FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON ... UNION SELECT ... FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON ...;
-- CROSS JOIN: har row x har row (cartesian), jaise dates x stations ka grid
SELECT d.day, s.id FROM calendar d CROSS JOIN stations s;
-- SELF JOIN: table apne aap se, jaise staff aur uska manager
SELECT e.name, m.name AS manager
FROM staff e LEFT JOIN staff m ON m.id = e.manager_id;
```
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: **INNER** = intersection, **LEFT** = left sab plus match, **anti-join** = LEFT plus `IS NULL`, **CROSS** = har combination.

q: Join andar se kaise chalta hai

- Join columns ka **data type same** ho (int ke saath int, same charset ke strings), warna index use nahi hota.
- Check kaise: `EXPLAIN`. Joined table par `type = ALL` ka matlab har row par full scan, yani index missing. `eq_ref` ya `ref` achhe signs hain.

q: NULL ka matlab "maloom nahi"
a:
NULL zero ya khali string nahi, "unknown" hai. Is liye:

- Division by zero se bachne ke liye: `amount / NULLIF(count, 0)` (zero ko NULL bana deta hai, to result NULL aata hai, error nahi).
- UNIQUE index mein kai NULL values allowed hain.

- **INNER vs LEFT JOIN?** INNER sirf matches, LEFT left ki saari rows aur match na ho to NULL.
- **LEFT JOIN mein WHERE se kya hota hai?** Right table par WHERE NULL rows nikaal ke INNER bana deta hai; condition ON mein rakho.
- **WHERE vs HAVING?** WHERE grouping se pehle rows filter, HAVING baad mein groups.
- **COUNT(\*) vs COUNT(col)?** Pehla sab rows, doosra sirf non-NULL.
- **UNION vs UNION ALL?** UNION duplicates hata deta hai (slow), UNION ALL sab rakhta hai (fast).
- **DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP?** Row-wise (rollback), poori table khali (implicit commit), table khatam.
- **PRIMARY vs UNIQUE?** Primary: ek hi, NOT NULL, clustered. Unique: kai ho sakte hain, NULL allowed.
- **Clustered vs secondary index?** Clustered mein table khud PK order mein; secondary mein PK ki value saath hoti hai.
- **NULL = NULL?** NULL, true nahi: `IS NULL` use karo.
- **Execution order?** FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
- **Join slow kyun?** Join column par index nahi, type mismatch, ya fan-out: EXPLAIN dekho.
- **Duplicates kaise dhoondte hain?** `GROUP BY col HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`.
- **Eloquent `with()` aur join mein farq?** `with()` do alag queries hain (models plus relations), join ek query hai (columns, filter, sort ke liye).

q: Har failure answer ka 4-step pattern

p: Failure-First Backend Interview What Happens When Things Fail (PHP Laravel)

q: **Prevent:** dobara na ho iske liye kya lagayenge? (idempotency, unique constraint, timeout, test)
a:
**Interviewer in cheezon ko dekhta hai:** kya aap partial failure samajhte hain, kya aap khud "idempotent?" ka sawal uthate hain, transaction ki hadd kahan hai (jo rollback nahi ho sakta, jaise bheja hua SMS), detection ka plan kya hai ("logs dekh lunga" kamzor jawab hai), aur recovery ka safe tareeqa kya hai.
**Agar aap ne aisa incident nahi dekha:** seedha kahein "mujhe production mein yeh nahi hua, lekin main yeh check karunga" aur reasoning dikhayen. Jhoota war story banane se behtar hai.
# Signature question
**F1. "Take a flow you built, like checkout or a signup email. Walk me through every step where it can fail halfway, and what state the system is left in each time."**
Yeh ek sawal bahut kuch check karta hai. Misaal: ticket checkout ke steps aur har step par failure:
| Step | Kya fail ho sakta hai | System kis state mein reh jata hai | Pata kaise chale | Recover aur prevent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Order `pending` banao aur seat hold karo | App crash order banane ke baad | Pending order aur seat hold, koi charge nahi | `pending` orders ki umar ki report | Scheduled job expired holds release kare |
| 2. Payment provider ko call | **Timeout: result maloom nahi** (paise kate ya nahi?) | Unknown state | Timeout metric aur alert | Blind retry nahi: idempotency key ke saath ya reconciliation se provider se asal status poochho |
| 3. Payment ho gayi, callback ya webhook gum | Network ya hamara server down | Provider ke yahan paid, hamare yahan pending | `pending` lekin provider mein `paid` ka mismatch report | Provider webhook retries plus reconciliation job |
| 4. Webhook 3 baar aaya | Duplicate delivery | Double confirm ya double SMS ka khatra | Duplicate event counters | Event ID par unique constraint, state transition idempotent |
| 5. Confirmation SMS ya email job | Provider down ya job crash | Order paid lekin user ko khabar nahi | Failed jobs aur queue age par alert | Backoff ke saath retries, `sent_at` flag, "resend" option |
| 6. Ticket PDF banana | Memory ya timeout | Ticket missing | Failed job alert | Retry, user ko "processing" dikhao, on-demand regenerate |
| 7. DB commit charge ke baad fail | DB error ya crash | **Paise kat gaye, local record nahi** | Reconciliation: provider ke paid orders jo hamare paas nahi | Charge se **pehle** local `pending` order likho (intent), taake hamesha record rahe |
**Kamzor answer:** "Try-catch laga dunga." **Mazboot answer:** har step par state, detection aur recovery batana, aur ye manna ke kuch cheezein (bheja hua SMS, kata hua paisa) rollback nahi hoti, isliye unke liye compensating action ya reconciliation chahiye.
**Follow-ups:** "Same webhook ek hi waqt mein do baar aaye to?" aur "Redis 30 second ke liye gayab ho to?" (F12 aur F21 dekhein).
# Section 1: Queue jobs aur retries
**F2. What happens if this queue job runs twice?** Answer: Pehle manta hoon ke yeh normal hai: queues "at-least-once" deliver karti hain, "exactly-once" nahi. Job do baar chal sakti hai jab: job `retry_after` se lambi chali aur wapas queue mein aa gayi, worker kaam ke beech mein crash ya OOM hua, deploy mein worker restart hua, ya kisi ne do baar dispatch kiya. Isliye job **idempotent** honi chahiye: start mein check (`if ($ticket->sms_sent_at) return;`), kaam, phir flag set. Pakka ilaaj database ka unique constraint ya state check hai, sirf code ka "if" kaafi nahi (race). Laravel mein `ShouldBeUnique` (dispatch duplicate rokta hai) aur `WithoutOverlapping` (ek hi key par ek waqt mein ek job) madad karte hain, lekin ye idempotency ka badal nahi.
**F3. A job exceeds its timeout but keeps running. Why do you see duplicates?** Answer: Queue config ka `retry_after` agar job ke `timeout` se chhota ya barabar ho, to queue samajhti hai job gum ho gayi aur use dobara de deti hai, jab ke pehla worker abhi chal raha hai: do workers ek hi job. Rule: `retry_after` hamesha job `timeout` se bara ho (aur worker ka `--timeout` job ke `timeout` se thoda bara). Aur timeout par job ko cleanly fail hona chahiye, adhi cheez chhor kar nahi, isliye kaam chhote hisson mein.
**F4. The worker crashes (OOM or deploy) in the middle of a job. What state is the system in?** Answer: Job ka jitna kaam ho chuka wo ho chuka (DB write, API call), baqi nahi, aur job wapas queue mein aayegi (retry\_after ke baad) aur dobara chalegi. Isliye har step ko "dobara chalane par safe" banana hai. DB kaam transaction mein (ya sab ya kuch nahi), aur external side effects (SMS, payment) ke liye idempotency key ya sent flag. Prevention: `--max-jobs`, `--memory` se workers ko khud restart, deploy par `queue:restart` (chalti job ko khatam hone dena), aur memory leak monitor.
**F5. A job fails every time (poison job). How do you stop it from clogging the queue?** Answer: Hamesha retry nahi: `$tries` aur `$maxExceptions` set, backoff (`[10, 60, 300]`) taake server par dabao na barhe, phir `failed_jobs` table mein. `failed(Throwable $e)` method mein alert ya compensating action. Failed jobs ki tadaad par alert, aur `queue:retry` tab jab bug theek ho chuka ho. Alag queues critical aur non-critical ke liye, taake ek kharab job important kaam na roke.
**F6. How do you make a "send SMS" job safe to retry?** Answer: Teen tareeqe mil kar: (1) database mein `sms_sent_at` ya per-message unique key (`ticket_id + type`) aur job ke shuru mein check, (2) provider ko idempotency key ya message reference dena agar wo support kare, (3) timeout par "result maloom nahi" ko alag handle (dobara bhejna double SMS bana sakta hai: business decide kare ke double SMS acceptable hai ya nahi). Sent flag ko SMS bhejne ke baad set karte hain, lekin crash flag aur SMS ke beech ho to ek duplicate ka imkan rehta hai: yeh "at-least-once" ki qeemat hai, isliye kuch messages (OTP) ke liye duplicates theek, kuch (paise) ke liye nahi.
**F7. A job is dispatched inside a transaction and runs before the commit. What happens?** Answer: Worker job uthata hai jab transaction abhi commit nahi hui, to `findOrFail` fail ya purana data. Fix: `->afterCommit()` ya queue config mein `after_commit => true`, taake job commit ke baad hi dispatch ho. Ulta masla bhi hai: commit ho gaya lekin dispatch fail (Redis down), to event kho gaya. Iske liye **outbox pattern**: event ko usi transaction mein ek `outbox` table mein likho, phir alag relay job usay queue mein bheje, taake DB aur queue ka "dual write" na toote.
**F8. After an outage, there are 2 lakh jobs in the backlog. What do you do?** Answer: Pehle dekhta hoon kya zaroori hai: purani jobs ab bhi kaam ki hain? (OTP ya "seat hold expiry" 2 ghante baad bekaar hai.) Time-sensitive jobs ke liye `retryUntil` ya expiry check taake purani jobs bina kaam kiye discard hon. Workers barhata hoon (lekin DB aur provider ke rate limits ka dhyan, warna backlog khatam karte karte DB gira dun), critical queues ko priority (`--queue=critical,default`), aur chhote batches mein dekhta hoon ke error rate na barhe. Baad mein: queue age (sab se purani job ki umar) par alert, taake backlog bante hi pata chale.
**F9. Jobs for the same ticket must run in order, but queues do not guarantee order. How do you handle it?** Answer: Pehle poochta hoon kya order sach mein zaroori hai. Agar haan: (1) ek ticket ki jobs ko chain (`Bus::chain`) mein rakho, (2) `WithoutOverlapping` ek key (`ticket:{id}`) par, (3) har event ko sequence number ya version do aur consumer purani ya out-of-order event ko ignore ya re-fetch kare, (4) ya state machine jo sirf valid transitions allow kare. Behtar design: aisi jobs banao jo order par depend na karein (current state read karke kaam karein).
**F10. How do you safely retry failed jobs after fixing a bug?** Answer: Pehle failed jobs ko dekhta hoon (kitni, kis wajah se), fix deploy, phir chhote batch par `queue:retry` ke saath nigrani. Jobs idempotent hon to retry safe. Agar adhi hui jobs ka state ghalat hai to pehle data repair script. Retry se pehle dekhta hoon ke jobs ab bhi relevant hain, aur rate limit ka khayal.
**F11. What is the difference between `tries`, `maxExceptions`, `backoff` and `retryUntil`?** Answer: `tries` job ki kul koshishein. `maxExceptions` itni exceptions ke baad fail (jab `tries` zyada hon lekin job manually `release()` bhi hoti ho). `backoff` retries ke beech ka waqfa (exponential, taake provider ya DB ko saans mile). `retryUntil` time-based hadd (is waqt ke baad retry nahi). Maslan payment reconciliation job ke liye `retryUntil` 24 ghante, OTP job ke liye `tries = 1` ya bohat chhota time window.
# Section 2: Idempotency, duplicates aur webhooks
**F12. The payment provider sends the same webhook three times. What happens in your system?** Answer: Pehle manta hoon duplicates normal hain (provider retry karta hai agar hamara jawab late ya fail ho). Design: webhook ki `event_id` ko `webhook_events` table mein **unique constraint** ke saath insert karo. Pehli baar insert hua to process, duplicate insert par unique violation pakad kar sirf `200 OK` wapas (dobara process nahi). Processing khud idempotent: "order ko `paid` karo" sirf tab jab abhi `pending` ho (state transition). Signature verify pehle, kaam queue mein, jawab jaldi (2xx).
**F13. Webhooks arrive out of order (for example refund before paid). How do you handle it?** Answer: Order par bharosa nahi karte. Har event mein provider ka timestamp ya sequence ho to us se compare; warna state machine sirf valid transitions allow kare aur out-of-order event ko park kare (retry baad mein) ya provider API se current status fetch kar ke us par amal. Source of truth provider ka current status hota hai, event sirf ishara.
**F14. The webhook arrives before your database transaction has committed. What happens?** Answer: Webhook handler order ko dhoondta hai lekin abhi commit nahi hua, to "order not found". Fix: order pehle commit hoga aur phir payment call (intent pehle likho), aur agar phir bhi "not found" aaye to 404 ke bajaye retryable jawab (5xx) ya job ko thodi der baad dobara chalao taake provider retry kare. Isi liye payment call kabhi uncommitted transaction ke andar nahi.
**F15. The payment succeeded at the provider but your callback never came. What do you do?** Answer: Order `pending` rehta hai. Do chizein: provider ke webhook retries, aur hamari **reconciliation job**: har kuch minute mein purane `pending` orders ke liye provider API se status poochho (order reference ya idempotency key se) aur `paid` ho to confirm, `failed` ho to release. Alert: "provider mein paid lekin hamare yahan 15 minute se pending". Yeh job hamesha chalni chahiye, kyunke webhooks par poora bharosa nahi.
**F16. A user double-clicks "Pay", or the mobile app retries the POST. What happens?** Answer: Client side button disable madad karta hai lekin server par bharosa nahi. Server: client se **idempotency key** (ek payment attempt ki ek key), jo server (`idempotency_keys` table, unique) mein result ke saath store ho; dohrai request wohi result lautaye aur dobara charge na ho. Aur database-level protection: `(order_id)` par unique payment ya order ki state check taake ek order ek hi baar paid ho.
**F17. How do you design an idempotency key?** Answer: Client har logical operation ke liye ek UUID banata hai aur retries mein wohi bhejta hai. Server key, user aur request ka hash store karta hai. Pehli request: kaam aur result save. Dohrai request wohi key: saved result return. Wohi key lekin alag payload: `409 Conflict` (ghalat istemal). Key ki TTL (jaise 24 ghante), aur save aur kaam ek transaction ya lock ke andar taake do ek saath requests dono nikal na jayein (unique constraint par ek jeete).
**F18. Webhook signature verification fails sometimes. What do you check?** Answer: Pehle unverified request ko process nahi karta (4xx, log). Phir wajah: signature **raw body** par hota hai (JSON parse ho kar dobara encode ho jaye to farq), server ka clock (timestamp tolerance), ghalat secret ya rotation, proxy ya middleware jo body badal de, aur environment (test secret vs live). Mismatch ki tadaad par alert (attack ya misconfiguration dono ka ishara).
**F19. Your endpoint is slow and the provider times out and retries. What do you do?** Answer: Webhook handler ko patla rakho: signature verify, event save (unique), job dispatch, `200` foran. Bhaari kaam queue mein. Warna provider timeout par retry karega aur load aur duplicates barhenge (retry storm).
**F20. How do you prove that no duplicate payment exists?** Answer: Do darje: (1) database constraints (payment reference par unique, order ek hi paid), (2) reconciliation report: hamari payments vs provider ki settlement file, mismatch ya duplicates list. Sirf code par bharosa nahi: constraint aur rozana reconciliation, aur alert agar mismatch aaye.
# Section 3: Redis aur cache failures
**F21. What if Redis is down for 30 seconds?** Answer: Pehle dekhta hoon Redis kis kaam mein hai: cache, session, queue, locks, rate limiting. Har ka asar alag: **Cache** down: reads database par girti hain (load barhta hai, error nahi agar fallback ho). **Sessions** Redis mein ho to users logout ya errors. **Queue** dispatch fail (events kho sakte hain: outbox pattern ya dispatch error par retry). **Locks** kaam nahi karenge (DB constraint ka final guard). **Rate limiting** fail-open ya fail-closed ka faisla. Design: cache ke liye fallback (naye Laravel versions mein failover cache aur queue drivers hain, apna version check karein), timeouts chhote taake requests latak na jayein, aur critical flows Redis par single point of failure na hon. Detection: Redis connection errors par alert, aur failover ka test.
**F22. Sessions are stored in Redis and Redis restarts. What do users experience?** Answer: Agar Redis mein persistence nahi to saari sessions kho jati hain: sab users logout, aur form ke beech wale users ka data (CSRF token) fail. Option: sessions ko database ya cookie mein, ya Redis mein AOF persistence aur replica. Aur login ke baad jaldi dobara login ka sehat-mand tajurba (data na khoye, saaf message).
**F23. A popular cache key expires and 1,000 requests hit the database at once. What is it called and how do you prevent it?** Answer: **Cache stampede (thundering herd).** Prevention: rebuild par `Cache::lock` taake ek request rebuild kare aur baqi purani value ya intezar karein, expiry mein random jitter taake bohat keys ek saath expire na hon, stale-while-revalidate (naye Laravel versions mein `Cache::flexible`), aur bohat hot keys ko background job se pehle hi refresh karna.
**F24. Redis memory fills up and starts evicting keys. Which keys are in danger?** Answer: Eviction policy par depend karta hai. `allkeys-lru` mein kuch bhi (queue ke jobs aur locks bhi!) nikal sakta hai, jo khatarnak hai. Isliye cache aur queues ke liye **alag Redis instance**: cache ke liye LRU eviction, queues aur locks ke liye `noeviction` (full ho to write error, jo silent loss se behtar hai). Memory aur eviction counters par alerts.
**F25. A Redis lock expires while the job is still working. What happens?** Answer: Doosra worker same lock le leta hai aur do jobs ek saath chal padti hain. Lock ko ek **hint** samjho, guarantee nahi: asal hifazat database ka unique constraint ya `lockForUpdate` hai. Mitigation: lock ki expiry kaam ke waqt se bara, lambe kaam ko chhote hisson mein, aur lock ko kaam ke dauran extend karna.
**F26. The cache serves stale data after an update. How do you find and fix it?** Answer: Pehle dekhta hoon update par key clear hui ya nahi (kisi ek code path par bhool), TTL kitni hai, aur kai servers ke local caches. Fix: jahan data likha jata hai wahin se invalidate (model observer ya event), versioned keys (`user:12:v3`), aur critical data (seats) par bohat chhoti TTL ya cache hi nahi, final check database se.
**F27. After Redis restarts, the cache is empty and the database is overwhelmed. What do you do?** Answer: **Cold cache** masla. Cache warm karna (critical keys pehle load), rebuild par lock (F23), rate limiting aur load shedding jab tak cache bhare, aur restart ko traffic kam waqt mein. Detection: restart ke baad database load aur latency alerts.
**F28. Redis fails over and some queued jobs are lost. How do you design for that?** Answer: Redis replication asynchronous hai, to failover mein aakhri writes kho sakti hain. Design: jobs idempotent, important events ke liye outbox (DB mein record, relay job queue mein daale), reconciliation jobs jo "jo hona chahiye tha lekin nahi hua" dhoondein (jaise paid order jis ka SMS nahi gaya), aur queues ke liye AOF persistence.
# Section 4: Database failures
**F29. A deadlock happens in production. What do you do?** Answer: MySQL ek transaction ko kill kar deta hai (error 1213) aur doosri chal jati hai. Laravel mein `DB::transaction(function () { ... }, 3)` deadlock par khud retry karta hai. Prevention: transactions chhoti, rows ko hamesha ek hi order mein lock karna, sahi indexes (kam rows lock hon), aur deadlock ki frequency par nazar. `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` se latest deadlock aur involved queries dekhta hoon.
**F30. A long-running worker starts failing with "MySQL server has gone away". Why?** Answer: Aam wajahein: connection idle rehne se server ke `wait_timeout` par band ho gayi, packet `max_allowed_packet` se bara, ya server restart hua. Laravel kuch lost-connection errors par ek baar reconnect kar leta hai, lekin lambe kaam (bahar ki API ka lamba intezar) ke dauran DB connection pakre rakhna masla banata hai. Fix: jobs chhoti, external call ke dauran transaction ya connection khuli nahi, zaroorat par `DB::reconnect()`, aur `wait_timeout` aur `max_allowed_packet` check.
**F31. A user saves a record and immediately sees old data. What is going on?** Answer: Shayad read replica lag: write primary par hui, read replica se hui jo abhi peeche hai. Laravel ke read/write config mein `'sticky' => true` (usi request mein write ke baad reads primary par). Agle requests ke liye critical reads primary par, ya write ke response mein hi naya data wapas dena. Replica lag par monitoring aur alert.
**F32. At peak time you get "Too many connections". How do you handle it?** Answer: Har FPM worker aur har queue worker ek connection pakadta hai: (FPM `max_children` x servers) plus queue workers `max_connections` se bara ho jata hai. Fix: sizing theek (connections ka hisaab), requests chhoti rakhna aur external calls ke dauran connection na pakadna, connection pooler (ProxySQL), `max_connections` sirf ek had tak barhana (RAM), aur connection usage percentage par alert.
**F33. A migration fails halfway on a huge production table. What state are you in?** Answer: MySQL mein DDL (ALTER, CREATE INDEX) implicit commit karta hai, to rollback nahi ho sakta: adhi tabdeeli reh sakti hai. Prevention: chhoti single-purpose migrations, production-size copy par pehle test, `php artisan migrate --pretend` se SQL dekhna, bade tables par online schema change tool (gh-ost), expand-then-contract (naya column nullable pehle, code badlo, purana baad mein), backup aur manual fix ka plan. Aur app code dono schema states par chalna chahiye.
**F34. A transaction does three writes and the third fails. What happens, and what about the email you already sent?** Answer: Teeno DB writes rollback ho jati hain (sab ya kuch nahi). Lekin transaction ke **andar** bheji hui email ya API call rollback nahi hoti, isliye side effects commit ke **baad** (`afterCommit`) ya outbox se. Agar kaam kai systems mein hai (DB plus provider), to saga: har step ka compensating action (refund, seat release).
**F35. Two requests try to create the same record at the same moment. What happens?** Answer: `if (!exists) create` mein race hai: dono "nahi hai" dekhte hain aur dono insert karte hain. Fix: database ka **unique constraint**, aur code mein duplicate-key exception pakad kar "pehle se hai" maan kar record fetch (`upsert` ya `firstOrCreate` ke saath constraint). Exception ka naam Laravel version par depend karta hai (naye versions mein `UniqueConstraintViolationException`).
**F36. The database server's disk is full. What do you do?** Answer: MySQL writes rok deta hai. Foran: jagah khali karna **safely**: purani binary logs (replication state dekh kar), slow aur general logs rotate, bade temp files. Data files kabhi delete nahi. Wajah dhoondna (data growth, binlogs, runaway table). Prevention: 70 aur 80 percent par alerts, growth rate ki nigrani, retention aur partition drop, aur binary log expiry.
**F37. A long report or an open transaction makes everything queue up. How do you find and fix it?** Answer: Lambi transaction ya report locks ya metadata lock pakre rakhti hai, aur doosri queries (khaas kar DDL) uske peeche latak jati hain. Dhoondna: `SHOW FULL PROCESSLIST` aur `information_schema.innodb_trx` (kaun si transaction kitni der se khuli). Foran: us session ko `KILL` (asar samajh kar). Prevention: heavy reports read replica par, transactions chhoti, query timeouts (`MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`), `lock_wait_timeout`, aur lambi transactions par alert.
**F38. Someone ran an UPDATE without a WHERE clause in production. What do you do?** Answer: Pehle damage rokta hoon (zaroorat ho to writes rok dein), phir point-in-time recovery se alag copy par restore kar ke sirf mutasir rows wapas laata hoon (poora production overwrite nahi). Prevention: production access mehdood, manual queries ka review ya peer check, `--safe-updates`, audit log, aur backup ka tested restore.
# Section 5: External APIs, timeouts aur partial failures
**F39. The payment or SMS provider becomes very slow. What happens to your web servers?** Answer: Har request jo us provider ko call kar rahi hai ek FPM worker pakad ke baithi rehti hai. Saare workers phans jayen to poori site slow ya down ho jati hai, un pages ke liye bhi jo provider se related nahi. Fix: chhote timeouts (`Http::timeout(5)->connectTimeout(2)`), jahan mumkin ho call queue mein (user ko "processing"), circuit breaker, aur alag queue ya pool taake ek provider poori site na girae (bulkhead).
**F40. The provider recovers and all your retries hit it at once. What is that and how do you prevent it?** Answer: **Retry storm.** Prevention: exponential backoff **plus jitter** (random delay), retries ki tadaad aur total waqt par hadd, queue concurrency aur rate limit (`RateLimited` job middleware), aur circuit breaker jo recovery par thoda thoda traffic bhejta hai (half-open).
**F41. What is a circuit breaker, and how would you build one in Laravel?** Answer: Teen states: **closed** (normal), **open** (lagataar failures ke baad kuch der call hi nahi, foran fail ya fallback), **half-open** (thoda traffic bhej kar check). Laravel mein jobs ke liye `ThrottlesExceptions` middleware (baar baar exception par job ko kuch der ke liye rok deta hai). HTTP calls ke liye apna chhota breaker: cache mein failure counter aur "open until" time, aur call se pehle check. Faida: provider ko recover hone ka moqa, aur hamare workers phansate nahi.
**F42. A payment call times out. Did the charge happen?** Answer: Pata nahi, aur yehi sab se khatarnak state hai. Timeout ka matlab "naakam" nahi, "result maloom nahi". Isliye blind retry nahi (double charge ka khatra). Order ko `unknown` ya `pending_verification` mein rakho, provider se idempotency key ya order reference se asal status poochho, aur reconciliation job se tay karo. Payment calls hamesha idempotency key ke saath.
**F43. The SMS gateway is down for an hour. What happens to the messages?** Answer: Queue mein rukti hain aur backoff ke saath retry. Lekin har message ki zaroorat alag: OTP ki expiry 5 minute hai, ek ghante baad bhejna bekaar, to `retryUntil` ya expiry check. Backup provider (adapter pattern se doosra gateway) par failover, OTP ko priority queue, aur alert jab failure rate barhe. Important messages (ticket confirmation) kho nahi jaane chahiyein: queue persistent aur reconciliation.
**F44. A bulk import of 1 lakh rows fails at row 60,000. What now?** Answer: Aisa design jo **resumable** ho: file ko staging table mein, batches mein process (har batch ke liye chhoti transaction), har row ka status (`done`, `failed`, `reason`), upsert natural key par (dobara chalane se duplicate nahi), checkpoint (kahan tak ho chuka), aur downloadable error report. Ek giant transaction nahi (lock aur memory). Laravel mein `Bus::batch()` jisme `allowFailures()` ho.
**F45. A third-party API changes its response format without notice. How do you cope?** Answer: Adapter layer jo response ko apne DTO mein badalta hai aur **shape validate** karta hai; validation fail ho to saaf error aur alert (silently ghalat data nahi). Contract tests ya recorded samples, vendor ko written report, aur graceful degradation (fallback ya "service temporarily unavailable") jab tak fix na ho.
# Section 6: Deploy, release aur scheduler failures
**F46. A deploy goes bad. How fast can you roll back?** Answer: Immutable releases (har release alag folder) aur `current` symlink: wapas switch seconds ka kaam. Lekin rollback tabhi chalta hai jab DB migrations **backward-compatible** hon (expand-then-contract). Feature flags (nayi cheez band kar do bina deploy), canary (pehle chhote hisse par), aur rollback ka criteria pehle se tay (jaise error rate itna ho to wapas). Rollback ki baqaida practice.
**F47. You rolled the code back, but the migration already dropped a column. What now?** Answer: Phans gaye. Isi liye destructive change (column drop) kabhi usi release mein nahi jis mein code badla: do step. Pehle code ko column istemal karna band karwao aur deploy, kuch din baad column drop. Rollback plan ke baghair destructive migration nahi.
**F48. After a deploy, queue workers are still running old code. Is there anything else to worry about?** Answer: Haan, workers long-running hain, to `queue:restart` (ya Horizon terminate) har deploy par. Aur ek aur baat: queue mein pehle se pade jobs **serialized** hote hain purani class ke saath. Agar nayi release mein job class ka structure badla (property ka naam, constructor), to purani jobs unserialize ya process par fail ho jati hain. Isliye job classes backward-compatible rakhein (naye fields optional), ya deploy se pehle queue drain karein.
**F49. After the deploy the app behaves oddly: missing env values or stale config. What happened?** Answer: `php artisan config:cache` ke baad `env()` sirf config files ke andar kaam karta hai; code mein jahan jahan `env()` seedha use hua wahan `null` aata hai. Aur purana cached config ya route cache naye code ke saath mismatch. Fix: `env()` sirf config files mein, deploy script mein ek hi tarteeb (`config:cache`, `route:cache`, `view:cache`, `event:cache`), aur deploy ke baad smoke test aur health check.
**F50. The scheduler runs the same task on two servers, or a task overlaps itself. How do you prevent it?** Answer: Kai servers par har ek par cron hota hai, to `->onOneServer()` (is ke liye shared cache jo locks support kare, jaise Redis ya database). Overlap ke liye `->withoutOverlapping(10)`: 10 minute ki expiry dein, warna crash ke baad lock bohat der atka reh sakta hai. Behtar: scheduler ek dedicated server par aur task idempotent.
**F51. A scheduled job silently stopped running three days ago. How would you know, and how do you prevent it?** Answer: Silently band hone ka pata nahi chalta kyunke koi error aata hi nahi. Isliye **dead man's switch**: har kamyab run par ek monitor ko ping (`->pingOnSuccess($url)`), aur monitor alert de agar ping na aaye (healthchecks.io jaisi service ya `spatie/laravel-schedule-monitor`). Saath mein: deploy ya server rebuild ke baad cron entry maujood honi chahiye (check), aur last-run time ka dashboard.
**F52. During a rolling deploy, some servers run the new version and some run the old. What breaks?** Answer: Load balancer ke peeche kuch der dono versions saath chalte hain. Todne wali cheezein: DB schema jo sirf naye code ke liye ho, API response ka format badalna, cache keys ya session format ka badalna, aur assets ke naam. Isliye har release dono versions ke saath chalne layak (backward-compatible DB aur API, versioned cache keys, hashed assets), aur ek ek server drain kar ke deploy.
# Section 7: Detection aur observability
**F53.
